sample_unit: dermatology cases (smartphone images from the SCIN dataset)

links.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy differences by Fitzpatrick skin tone (light vs dark) across four chatbots
links.effect: Top-1 disparity significant only for Grok (56.0% light vs 45.1% dark skin, p = 0.007); top-3 disparities significant for Claude, Gemini and Grok.
links.quote: For top-1 accuracy, Fitzpatrick skin tone disparity was significant only for Grok, the best-performing model (56.0% light versus 45.1% dark skin, p = 0.007), whereas top-3 disparities were significant for Claude, Gemini and Grok.

unlisted_practices: Adding clinical context to image inputs improved accuracy only for Grok (+5.5%) and GPT (+3.8%); removing images caused 11-18 percentage point losses
Inter-model agreement was low across image-based analyses (Fleiss' kappa 0.34-0.41)

screen.reason: Evaluates the diagnostic accuracy and equity across skin tones of four multimodal consumer AI chatbots on the benchmark SCIN dermatology dataset under different input conditions.
